title: HTTP & HTTPS Revision Notes
summary: Quick revision notes on the HTTP request/response model, methods, status codes, headers, HTTP/1.1 vs 2 vs 3, cookies, and HTTPS with the TLS handshake and certificate authorities.

chapters.title: HTTP Mental Model
points: HTTP is a stateless, text-based request/response protocol: the client sends one request, the server returns one response, and the server keeps no memory between requests
Request = start line (METHOD /path HTTP/1.1) + headers + blank line + optional body
Response = status line (HTTP/1.1 200 OK) + headers + blank line + optional body
A URL splits into scheme://host:port/path?query#fragment; the fragment is never sent to the server
Default ports: HTTP 80, HTTPS 443; statelessness is why cookies and tokens exist

chapters.title: Methods and Status Codes
points: GET reads, POST creates or triggers, PUT replaces the whole resource, PATCH changes part of it, DELETE removes it
Safe methods (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) don't change state; idempotent methods (GET, PUT, DELETE) give the same result when repeated; POST is neither
Status classes: 1xx informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error
Key codes: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 301 permanent redirect, 302 temporary redirect, 304 Not Modified
Key errors: 400 bad request, 401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not found, 429 rate limited, 500 server bug, 502 bad gateway, 503 unavailable, 504 gateway timeout

chapters.title: Headers and Cookies
points: Request headers: Host (required in HTTP/1.1), User-Agent, Accept, Authorization: Bearer <token>, Content-Type (body format, e.g. application/json)
Response headers: Content-Type, Content-Length, Location (used with 3xx), Cache-Control (e.g. max-age=3600), ETag (validator; client revalidates with If-None-Match and gets 304)
A server sets a cookie with Set-Cookie: id=abc; the browser then sends Cookie: id=abc on every matching request
Cookie flags: HttpOnly (hidden from JavaScript), Secure (HTTPS only), SameSite=Lax/Strict (limits cross-site sending, defends against CSRF), Max-Age/Expires, Path/Domain
Common mistake: storing session tokens in cookies without HttpOnly + Secure + SameSite, or sending credentials in a URL query string

chapters.title: HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3
points: HTTP/1.1: text protocol over TCP, one request at a time per connection (head-of-line blocking), browsers open ~6 parallel connections per host; keep-alive reuses connections
HTTP/2: binary framing over TCP, multiplexes many streams on one connection, HPACK header compression; TCP-level head-of-line blocking remains
HTTP/3: runs over QUIC on UDP, so a lost packet stalls only its own stream; TLS 1.3 built in, faster handshake and connection migration
HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 are negotiated: HTTP/2 via ALPN during the TLS handshake, HTTP/3 advertised by the Alt-Svc header; semantics (methods, status codes, headers) are unchanged
Trade-off: HTTP/1.1 needs bundling and domain sharding for speed, while HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 make that unnecessary

chapters.title: HTTPS, TLS Handshake and Certificates
points: HTTPS = HTTP inside TLS, giving encryption, integrity and server authentication
TLS 1.3 handshake: ClientHello (versions, ciphers, key share) → ServerHello + certificate + key share → both derive session keys → Finished; takes 1 round trip
Asymmetric crypto and key exchange (ECDHE) set up the session; fast symmetric encryption (AES-GCM, ChaCha20) then carries the data; ephemeral keys give forward secrecy
A certificate binds a domain name to a public key and is signed by a certificate authority (CA); the browser validates the chain leaf → intermediate → root against its trusted root store
Certificate checks: signature chain, hostname match (SAN), validity dates, and revocation (OCSP/CRL); Let's Encrypt issues free 90-day certificates

chapters.title: HTTP Cheat Sheet
points: curl essentials: curl -i URL (show headers), curl -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"a":1}' URL, curl -v (shows TLS handshake and headers), curl -L (follow redirects), curl --http2 / --http3
Methods: GET read, POST create, PUT replace, PATCH partial, DELETE remove; idempotent = GET/PUT/DELETE
Status memory aid: 2xx ok, 3xx go elsewhere, 4xx your fault, 5xx server's fault; 401 = who are you, 403 = not allowed
Cookie flags to always set: HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; protocol versions: 1.1 TCP serial, 2 TCP multiplexed, 3 QUIC/UDP
Debug TLS: openssl s_client -connect host:443 -servername host shows the chain; common failures are expired cert, hostname mismatch, missing intermediate, untrusted CA
